minutes.headline: Committee finished editing its draft master-plan recommendations before sending them to the planning board
minutes.summary: In what was billed as its final meeting, the Master Plan Steering Committee went line-by-line through a spreadsheet of draft recommendations with consultants Ramy and Tristan, softening or consolidating wording on housing, farmland, school facilities, Lake Shirley access, town-owned parcels, business development and recreation. No formal votes were taken on the edits; the chair will compile outstanding meeting minutes and a list of past members, and the draft plan is expected to go to the planning board around mid-to-late January.

attendees.role: chair of the planning board (public comment)

public_comment.topic: Thanked the committee for a three-year effort and asked the chair to compile a list of current and past committee members so he could thank them by name at the planning board's next meeting.

votes.outcome: passed 6-0 (roll call: Teddy, Glenn, Emily, David, Tony, and chair all voted yes)

budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the town's current consultant contract, described as $42,000, is to help build the process for charging residents and businesses a stormwater utility fee.
It was said the task force may set a flat annual fee for all residences in a range described, while commercial/industrial fees would be based on impervious surface.
A member recalled that a grant used to fund half the cost of building dog parks, and that dog parks are described as wildly expensive at a figure given.

decisions.decision: Remove committees from the recommendations list that said the work doesn't fall in their purview, and combine remaining committee names into the 'required resources' column instead of a separate volunteers note.
Change the first-time homebuyer program recommendation to 'promote' rather than 'advertise,' and list only the Lunenburg Housing Authority as an owner, dropping other agencies.
Remove reference to TC Pacios from the town-center events-programming recommendation so it covers the town center more broadly.
Update Turkey Hill and other school-related recommendations to 'three-year' language per the school committee's request.
Reword the STEM recommendation to 'explore funding options for additional steam programs as part of school budget,' with STEAM defined in the text.
Change 'create a trades program' to 'explore options for creating greater opportunities for Lunenburg students to engage with trades programs,' since Monty Tech precludes a separate district program.
Reword the green-community recommendation to 'strive to maintain status as a green community' and specify it refers to the Massachusetts program.
Consolidate the Turkey Hill renovation and school-accessibility recommendations into one line about evaluating renovations to meet accessibility standards, removing the duplicate.
Leave the Brooks House out of the recommendations document, as it did not rank in the top building priorities.
Reword the Lake Shirley recommendation to 'maintain access to Lake Shirley for [Lunenburg] residents,' reflecting the resolved Shady Point agreement.

Simplify the 30 School Street recommendation to 'develop options for [the] parcel,' removing references to parking and green space, since it's covered by the broader town-property inventory recommendation.

Add the library to the list of components (with TC Pacios and Adult Activity Center) in the town-green/fire-lane recommendation, and fold the geogrid fire-lane detail into that recommendation's description rather than as a separate line.

Remove the duplicate community-garden line and the separate 'assess allowing public use of the greenhouse' line, keeping one recommendation to continue school gardening with a note that public use could follow if the school program ends.
Reword the assisted-living recommendation to 'assess the conditions that would allow for the development of' assisted living.
Reword the low-income senior housing recommendation similarly to 'assess the conditions that would allow the development of low-income senior housing.'
Consolidate two similar business-investment/zoning-barrier recommendations into one: 'assess existing bylaws and processes to reduce barriers to business development.'
Add wildlife-connectivity and native-landscaping/climate-resilience language into the recommendation guiding new development, rather than creating a new recommendation.
Limit the uniform town-signage recommendation to municipal buildings only, not private property.
Chair will send the draft recommendations spreadsheet to committee members and, once the plan draft is ready (expected mid-to-late January), circulate it before it goes to the planning board.

what_happened.line: The steering committee went line-by-line through its draft master-plan recommendations, softening or combining wording across housing, schools, farmland, Lake Shirley, town parcels, business and recreation, without taking a formal vote on any edit.

School-related recommendations were changed to match school committee feedback, including three-year language for Turkey Hill and folding a separate accessibility line into one renovation recommendation.
The Lake Shirley recommendation was reworded to say the town will maintain resident access, reflecting a resolved Shady Point agreement.
Housing recommendations were softened to say the town will 'assess the conditions' for assisted living and low-income senior housing rather than commit to developing them.
The committee treated this as its final working meeting; the chair will compile outstanding minutes and a list of members before the draft goes to the planning board.

why_it_matters: This is the wording the planning board will receive and act on for the town's next master plan, covering housing, schools, farmland, recreation and business development.
None of the edits were put to a formal vote, so the record of what changed rests on this meeting rather than on a roll call.
Recommendations on Turkey Hill, Lake Shirley access and senior/affordable housing options set the direction future boards will be asked to fund or zone for.
